title: Automated cost controls: change-approval guardrails and tamper-proof audit for auto-apply/rollback
creator: Asha Mehta
description:
Summary:
Design and implement security and compliance guardrails for the Cost Tuner automatic batching/caching recommendations pipeline. This ticket covers RBAC roles and enforcement, change-approval workflows, immutable audit trail & tamper-evidence, safe apply/canary rollout semantics, and an automated but auditable rollback mechanism.

Goals:
- Allow automated cost-tuning recommendations to be applied in hosted/dedicated/private modes while meeting enterprise compliance requirements.
- Enforce least-privilege RBAC and separation-of-duties for auto-apply flows.
- Provide an indelible, queryable audit trail for every recommended change and rollback, with cryptographic signing of change artifacts.
- Detect and automatically revert unsafe changes via canary metrics while ensuring all rollbacks are logged and reviewed.

Non-goals:
- Model tuning algorithms themselves (this ticket focuses on governance and infra around apply/rollback).

Proposed design (high level):
1) RBAC model and enforcement:
   - New roles: CostTunerAdmin (create/approve/apply/revert), CostTunerOperator (propose/dry-run), CostTunerAuditor (read-only audit access).
   - Integrate with SSO/SCIM groups; map enterprise groups to roles.
   - Enforcement at the orchestration API layer: every apply/rollback request requires an auth token checked against role and resource scope (project, cluster, model).

2) Change approval flow:
   - Two-stage approval for auto-apply in customer-managed or enterprise orgs: automated proposal -> security/ops approval -> scheduled apply.
   - For low-risk namespaces (internal sandbox), allow operator-level auto-apply with strict monitoring enabled.
   - Approvals recorded as signed artifacts (JSON blob with change diff, approver, timestamp) signed using KMS/HSM key for tamper evidence.

3) Immutable audit & tamper-evidence:
   - Store every proposal/approval/apply/rollback as an append-only event in the audit store. Events include: diff, pre-state checksum, post-state checksum, metrics baseline, and signer identity.
   - Use a signing key (KMS/HSM) to produce a digest for each event and persist digest in the log and in an external WORM log (e.g., cloud retention ledger or dedicated audit service).
   - Provide export endpoints for compliance teams (CSV/JSON) and retention policy controls.

4) Safe apply/canary/rollback semantics:
   - All applies go through canary by default: 1% traffic or small pool for 30m with pre-defined success criteria (latency, error-rate, token-per-second cost delta thresholds).
   - Canary failure triggers automatic rollback; rollback is executed as a new signed change event and annotated in the audit trail with root-cause signals.
   - For automated periodic tuning jobs, require evidence from dry-run simulations against historical traces before auto-applying.

5) Change management integration and traceability:
   - Link proposals to GitHub PR or ticket ID (e.g., config-as-code change) and surface links in the audit UI.
   - Emit telemetry events to Console for per-route/model dashboards and for SLA billing reconciliation.

6) Monitoring, alerts, and SLOs:
   - New alerts for: unauthorized apply attempts, approval delays >24h, canary failure rate >2x expected, rollback frequency >3% per week.
   - Metrics to surface: apply success rate, mean time to rollback, number of signed approvals, number of auto-applies vs manual applies, cost delta pre/post apply.

Security & compliance considerations:
- Separation of duties: approvals must come from a different principal than the proposer (enforced by RBAC/SCIM mapping).
- Key management: signing keys stored in customer-managed KMS for Private deployments; Redwood KMS for Hosted with HSM-backed keys. Key rotation plan and emergency key-rotation playbook included.
- Data retention: default 365 days for audit artifacts; allow enterprise overrides to 7 years via release add-on.
- Tamper detection: periodic audit job validates digests and alerts on mismatch.
- GDPR/Export: ensure audit export contains only permitted PII; provide redaction option and retention policies.

Testing & validation plan:
- Unit tests for RBAC checks and signing flow.
- E2E test harness simulating canary apply and induced failures to verify rollback and audit entries.
- Load test for audit log ingestion to verify append-only latency under 1k/sec spikes.
- Compliance review & tabletop exercise with security team.

Rollout plan:
- Phase 1 (internal): enable in staging and internal orgs with CostTunerOperator role; require manual approval for production applies.
- Phase 2 (beta customers): opt-in for enterprise orgs with security review; enable automated dry-run evidence requirement.
- Phase 3 (GA): default on for Hosted with approved defaults; Private deployments respect customer KMS and retention settings.

Open questions / trade-offs:
- How heavy should the approval UX be for PLG users vs enterprise tenants? (Trade-off between safety and speed.)
- Append-only store choice: use existing Console event store with signed blobs vs separate immutable ledger service. Console reuse is faster; separate ledger is stronger for compliance and isolation.
- Signing strategy: per-event signing vs batch-signing to reduce KMS DT. Batch reduces cost but weakens per-event cryptographic granularity.

Dependencies:
- ENG-11702 (autopolicy access control & audit trail) -- integration dependency.
- ENG-9083 (secure autodeploy cost optimizer RBAC/audit) -- reference for RBAC patterns.
- infra/kms-integration epic (teams: infra/security) for HSM/KMS support.

Acceptance criteria:
- RBAC roles implemented and enforced at orchestration API layer.
- Approval flow implemented with signed approval artifacts stored in audit log.
- Canary apply + automatic rollback executed end-to-end in staging with audit entries present for each step.
- Audit log retention configurable and exportable; digests validated by periodic job.

Documentation & artifacts:
- Design doc (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INFR/Cost+Tuner+Governance+and+Audit
- PR for PoC signing: https://github.com/redwood-inference/policies/pull/467
- Prototype audit viewer: https://console.redwood.ai/audit-demo

Notes:
- This ticket ties directly into broader cost-optimizer automation work; we must avoid duplicating policy enforcement code. Plan to extract a small authorization+signing library for reuse across deploy pipelines.
comments: 2026-02-11: Spike complete - PoC for KMS-signed approval artifacts using hosted KMS. Proof shows <50ms overhead per sign; need cost estimate for heavy signing workloads.
2026-02-15: Security review - require separation of duties: approver cannot be the same identity as proposer. Security asked for HSM-backed keys for production applies in Hosted.
2026-02-25: Eng sync - agreed on default canary size 1% or a dedicated small worker pool for traffic-insensitive workloads. Added dry-run requirement for scheduled tuning jobs.
2026-03-03: PM feedback - need configurable retention per org and an export for SOC teams. Also requested audit CSV format and a retention policy UI in Console.
2026-03-05: Added integration tickets: infra/kms-integration and console/audit-export. Assigned infra lead to coordinate HSM provisioning for GA.
2026-03-09: QA note - E2E canary+rollback test failing intermittently under synthetic traffic. Investigating race between apply completion and metrics window; tentative fix to extend window by 10m.
2026-03-10: Security approved design in principle pending KMS/HSM proofs and the tabletop exercise scheduled for 2026-03-18.
